intro: Work and experiments across landscapes, sculpture, medicine, archives, and the things that happen between them.
bio:
Lauren Yoon Kim (she/her) is an artist and researcher working across installation, sculpture, and writing. She is one half of Cloud6, an ongoing collaboration with Jane Zhang. Their work has been presented at the Goethe-Institut Los Angeles, ArtSpace HP, and Yale Peabody Museum. Alongside Enoch Ma and her father, acupuncturist Han Jik Kim, Cloud6 created Inner Landscapes: A Pulse Reading of MacArthur Park, an exhibition that reimagined the park through the diagnostic practices of traditional East Asian medicine.

Informed by her background in urban planning and land conservation, she is drawn to the peculiar instruments, rituals, and systems of knowledge through which people have learned to observe and interpret the world around them. Moving between archival research and speculative invention, she borrows from these traditions of observation to create sculptural objects and immersive environments. Through playful shifts in scale and material experimentation, she explores how careful observation can give rise to myth, wonder, and other ways of imagining our place in the world.
